commits.message:
fix(ci): run the demo gate on the publish path (rich-workflows-0pr.1) (#125)

publish.yml ran lint, test, and build, then published — never the docs build or
the headless-browser demo gate that ci.yml treats as required on master. Neither
lint nor test touches the bundle pipeline, so a change breaking every browser
demo cleared the release gate and shipped to npm with provenance attached.

The checks now live in .github/actions/gate, a composite action with no inputs,
and both workflows call it. Copying ci.yml's steps into publish.yml would have
scheduled the same bug again: the two lists drifted by omission, and a second
copy drifts the same way on the path nobody watches.

Review raised that this widened the blast radius of id-token: write, since the
gate brought vite/vitepress, a Chromium download, and real headless execution
into the job holding the npm Trusted Publishing credential. permissions is
granted per job, so publish.yml is now two jobs: gate (contents: read, no
id-token) runs the checks and the build and hands dist/ forward as an artifact;
publish (needs: gate, id-token: write) holds checkout, setup-node, the npm CLI
upgrade, the artifact download, the tag/version check, and npm publish. No
npm ci there — nothing on that path needs node_modules, and installing would
run every devDependency's install scripts inside exactly the job the split
protects.

The split's own fallout is folded in: one workflow-level Node pin read by both
jobs instead of two literals, and no npm cache on the job that never installs.

Verified: actionlint clean, the gate's step list green locally (lint, 2471 unit
tests, docs:build, 10 browser demos), and CI ran the composite on a real runner.
Proving the failure direction end to end is rich-workflows-0pr.3; Node
resolution from engines across all three workflows is rich-workflows-0pr.2.
